chunks: O you who believe, may I offer you a bargain which will save you from a painful punishment?

key_terms.أَدُلُّكُمْ: I guide you or show you the way
key_terms.تِجَارَة: Trade or commercial transaction, used metaphorically for spiritual investment
key_terms.عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ: Painful punishment, referring to the consequences of disbelief or hypocrisy

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual trade that saves believers from painful punishment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a divine invitation to the 'trade' of sacrificing one's wealth and self in the path of Allah, with Imam Ali (AS) frequently cited as the prime exemplar of this spiritual commerce. It underscores the concept of *Jihad* not merely as physical struggle but as a transactional exchange where believers trade their worldly assets for eternal salvation, a theme deeply resonant with the Shia understanding of *Fada'il* (virtues) and self-sacrifice. This invitation sets the stage for the subsequent description of those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, highlighting the necessity of sincere commitment (*Sidq*) in faith.
